endorsements.quote: Thus, it is crucial that a “human‐in‐the‐loop” (HITL) model is utilized to guard against inaccurate documentation, 35 which can lead to incorrect or even harmful treatment and paradoxically, decreased efficiency of chart review.
Robust studies are also necessary to establish standards for model accuracy across diverse patient populations as well as standards for training data.
This may be mitigated by ensuring that training data meet certain metrics of equitable representation, which will have to be delineated.

Therefore, training the epileptologist to “periodically summarize” key points of seizure history during the clinical encounter may be effective in gathering accurate information that is void of much fabrication.

The utilization of these models, however, requires a HITL design to ensure adequate quality of output as well as continued monitoring that, if ignored, could ultimately jeopardize patient safety in epilepsy clinical practice.
Future prospective studies must be undertaken to concretely establish the advantages of using AmI models.

unlisted_practices: Mitigate bias in speech recognition software used by ambient AI models, including for accents, speech impediments, dysarthria, and interpreter-mediated encounters.
Develop regulatory guidelines for software and algorithms critical to clinical workflow that do not meet criteria as medical devices.
Epileptologists, clinical informaticists, programmers, and policymakers should collaborate to produce policy and regulations on AI use in clinical practice that safeguard patient safety and privacy.
Use structured documentation for information poorly suited to verbal review, such as the history of antiseizure medications trialed and failed, to supplement ambient AI notes.
Ensure ambient AI systems demonstrate secure handling, storage, and transmission of PHI, and disclose encryption methods, access controls, and de-identification procedures to regulators.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article examining the challenges, risks, and governance considerations of deploying ambient intelligence documentation tools in outpatient epilepsy care.
